key_insight: JUCAL is a post-hoc calibration method that jointly calibrates aleatoric (data) and epistemic (model) uncertainty in classifier ensembles, producing more balanced and accurate predictive probabilities than methods that treat uncertainty monolithically.
problem_solved: Standard calibration techniques (e.g., temperature scaling, conformal methods) do not distinguish or balance aleatoric and epistemic contributions, causing misattributed uncertainty and suboptimal decision thresholds for downstream tasks; this paper provides a way to correct that at the ensemble level after training.
method: Decompose ensemble predictive uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components (e.g., via predictive entropy and inter-model variance) to quantify each source separately.

Optimize a joint, post-hoc calibration transform that adjusts the balance between aleatoric and epistemic terms (e.g., separate scaling/temperature factors or a small calibration network) using a validation set or holdout conformal-style procedure.
Evaluate calibration and coverage metrics for both components and tune transforms to improve overall reliability while preserving sharpness and coverage guarantees.
impact: By yielding better-separated and calibrated uncertainty estimates, JUCAL improves trustworthiness for risk-sensitive applications (e.g., medical diagnosis, autonomous systems), enhances OOD detection and active learning, and can be applied to existing trained ensembles without retraining.

paper_title: JUCAL: Jointly Calibrating Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty in Classification Tasks
paper_authors: Jakob Heiss, Sören Lambrecht, Jakob Weissteiner, Hanna Wutte, Žan Žurič
